minutes.headline: Commission voted down a sewer easement waiver for the 763 Massachusetts Ave duplex project
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission held a continued public hearing on a waiver/easement request for a 763 Massachusetts Avenue project converting a funeral home into duplexes, ultimately voting to deny the waiver over concerns about setting a precedent for easements instead of requiring direct street tie-ins. The commission also voted to adopt an ADU sewer connection charge policy, discussed an extension for a manhole-replacement contractor, and agreed to explore requiring future sewer connections to run to a property's own street rather than through easements.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted down a sewer easement waiver for the 763 Massachusetts Ave duplex conversion project.
All members present voted against the waiver, denying the developer's request to use an easement instead of a direct street tie-in.
The commission adopted a new one-time connection charge policy for accessory dwelling units, based on Title 5 flow.
Members agreed to draft a future regulation requiring sewer connections to run to a property's own street rather than through an easement.
The commission granted the manhole-replacement contractor an extension to June 30, 2026, since roads cannot be reopened after mid-November.

why_it_matters: The denied waiver means the 763 Massachusetts Ave duplex project cannot proceed with an easement-based sewer connection and would need a different, likely costlier, tie-in approach.
A future regulation requiring direct street tie-ins instead of easements could affect how other properties near shared sewer mains are allowed to connect going forward.
Owners adding accessory dwelling units will now face a one-time sewer connection charge calculated per gallon under Title 5 flow standards.
watch_next: A future Sewer Commission agenda item drafting the street-tie-in-only regulation

They differ mostly in detail: our minutes carry caption-garbled cost figures and an inferred ADU agenda decision, and the official minutes carry the minutes-approval vote, the rate-increase discussion and the Town Meeting note. The thing to check is the decisions we recorded (manhole extension, drafting a regulation, keeping the ADU item off agendas), which the official minutes describe as reports or discussion with no motion.
